title: Design, synthesis, and bioevaluation of novel unsaturated cyanoacetamide derivatives
author: Uddin, Meem, et al.
materials: Table 3 reveals that among all the compounds, compound 5 exhibited the largest HOMO-LUMO gap value (3.753 eV), highest hardness (1.886 eV), and lowest softness (0.530 eV). This can be attributed to its 3,4-methylenedioxybenzylidene ring, setting it apart from the other compounds. When comparing the HOMO-LUMO gaps of the reference compound AG99 and compound 5, they display similar characteristics, but AG99 has a slightly higher gap than compound 5, suggesting better stability and reactivity. Furthermore, the reaction involving compound 5 has led to a reduced HOMO-LUMO gap and a lower dipole moment (2.927 D), indicative of improved biological activities. The energy gap values decrease as follows: 5 (3.753 eV) > AG99 (3.896 eV) > 2 (3.997 eV) > 3 (4.036 eV) > 4 (4.043 eV) > 1 (4.064 eV). The higher global softness of compound 5 aligns well with the results obtained for antibacterial activities (Table 3). Similarly, compound AG99 exhibits stronger reactivity regarding the electronic chemical potential (µ) than compound 5. This parameter can be used to gauge the reactivity of molecules, with reactivity increasing as chemical potentials decrease. Additionally, the electrophilicity index (ω) parameter indicates that compound 5 possesses a higher electrophilicity index (2.616 eV) than all the synthesized compounds, implying its ability to accept electrons [65]. Molecular docking with a suitable protein may offer further insights into these potential activities.

steps.title: Optimize geometries and compute electronic properties
steps.instruction: Use Gaussian16 to optimize the molecular geometry of each compound at the B3LYP/6‑31G(d,p) level; perform Frontier Molecular Orbital (FMO) calculations to obtain HOMO and LUMO energies; generate molecular electrostatic potential (MEP) maps with GaussView 6; calculate the descriptors EGap, IP, EA, χ, µ, η, σ, and ω using the equations EGap = ELUMO – EHOMO, IP = –EHOMO, EA = –ELUMO, χ = (IP+EA)/2, µ = –χ, η = (IP–EA)/2, σ = 1/η, ω = µ²/(2η).

steps.title: Perform single‑point energy and NBO analysis
steps.instruction: Run single‑point energy calculations and natural bond orbital (NBO) analysis on the optimized structures in Gaussian16 to obtain potential energies and atomic charges.

steps.title: Prepare ligand files for docking
steps.instruction: Download 3‑D SDF files of the derivatives and reference drugs from PubChem; open each in GaussView 6 and re‑optimize at B3LYP/6‑31G(d,p) with Gaussian16; perform energy minimization; convert the minimized structures to PDBQT format using the OpenBabel plugin of PyRx 0.8.

steps.title: Prepare protein structures for docking
steps.instruction: Retrieve the eight target proteins (PDB IDs: 6SE1, 5GVZ, 5N1J, 4NZZ, 7FEQ, 5MM8, 5XVU, 1TM2) from the RCSB PDB; open each in Chimera 1.16, delete all water molecules and bound ligands, and perform energy minimization; set the appropriate protonation state for histidine residues; assign the default AMBER ff14SB force field to all residues; calculate Gasteiger charges for all other residues.
